description:
"Where does this operation's failure go" (raise through ctx, a speculated select's flag, a guard's bad/ovf/stop flag, a strip's deferred check) is answered from three state homes and a C suffix: `env.case_guard` and `env.ovf` (`checked/1` ~L2956, `checked_float/1`, `guarded/2` ~L2325, `guard?/flagged?` ~L5422), `low(:guard)` (`guard_expr`), and `_s(&` which `Defk.Strip.classify` recognises later by token scan. Every arithmetic emitter must pick the right one of `checked`/`checked_float`/`guarded`.

Settled shape (grilling 2026-10-19):
- env carries `sink: :raise | {:select, flag} | {:guard, scope}`.
- One function `check(sink, kind)` with `kind` in `:ovf | :bad | :stop` returns the C prefix and declares the strip row; `checked/1`, `checked_float/1`, `flagged_check/1` and `guarded/2` become its clauses.
- `guard_expr`, `select` and the strips construct sinks. The sink replaces `env.ovf` and `env.case_guard` as the only marker: `guard?/1` and `flagged?/1` read the sink.
- CONTEXT.md gains the term "Error sink" (where a kernel's failed check goes: a raise, a select's flag, a guard's flag, a strip's deferred test). docs/agents/compiler-map.md: the "case" and "expressions" rows.
- Adjacent to x3a.6 (guard flags as locals): that settled the storage, this is the dispatch.

Tests: case_guard_errors_test ~L562-678, bitwise_test ~L239-241, early_exit_test ~L384 grep `_s(&`/`_g(&` (about 12 lines); a sink's decision is observable as a `:check` note.

Gate: byte-identical `mix dump_c`; `mix ci`; PR per AGENTS.md.

comments.text: PR #60: env.sink + check/2; guard flags stay in the ctx (x3a.6); kept :check notes name the sink; C unchanged; mix ci green (2294 passed).

title: One error sink: where a failed check goes is one value in env
